title: An explanatory study of factors influencing engagement in AI education at the K-12 Level: an extension of the classic TAM model
extended_summary:
This paper examines what factors influence K-12 students’ engagement and attitudes toward AI education when learning with generative AI tools. The authors extend the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) by adding four cognitive factors—AI intrinsic motivation, AI readiness, AI confidence, and AI anxiety—and three human-computer interaction factors—user interface, content, and learner-interface interactivity—to explain perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and attitudes toward AI learning.

The study was conducted with 210 Chinese students in grades 7 to 9 who completed a one-month AI course. The course centered on creating AI-themed picture books and included use of ChatGPT, Midjourney, and AI translation tools. Students completed post-course questionnaires, and the authors analyzed the data using structural equation modeling. After screening, 197 valid responses were used in the final analysis.

Results showed that intrinsic motivation, readiness, confidence, interface quality, content quality, and learner-interface interactivity all positively predicted perceived usefulness and/or perceived ease of use, while AI anxiety had negative effects on both. Perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use, in turn, positively predicted attitudes toward learning AI. The paper concludes that both cognitive and interface-related factors matter for K-12 AI course acceptance and suggests that AI4K12 curriculum design should account for these dimensions.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed correlational SEM study with a clear survey-based methodology, but it is not an experimental or causal design. Credibility is limited for subgroup effects or learning gains because outcomes are attitudes and acceptance perceptions rather than academic achievement.
impact_tier_rationale: The study reports modest positive path coefficients for acceptance and attitude constructs, but these are not direct achievement effects. The impacts are meaningful for engagement and adoption of GenAI in K-12, yet they are indirect and based on self-report rather than performance gains.

interventions.use_case: GenAI-supported K-12 AI course activities using ChatGPT for generating narrative text, discussing AI concepts, and supporting students' creation of AI-themed picture books; Midjourney is also used as a generative AI companion for image creation in the same course.

finding.finding_summary: This correlational SEM study (valid n=197) found that students' AI intrinsic motivation, readiness, confidence, perceived usefulness, and perceived ease of use were positively associated with attitudes toward learning AI through GenAI, while AI anxiety was negatively associated. Reported path coefficients included AIIM→PU β=0.211, AIRD→PU β=0.152, AICF→PU β=0.158, AIAX→PU β=-0.130, and AIAX→PEOU β=-0.162; PU→ATT β=0.208 and PEOU→ATT β=0.228.
finding.measure: Survey-based TAM constructs: attitudes toward AI learning, perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, intrinsic motivation, readiness, confidence, and anxiety
finding.effect_size: β=0.211 to -0.162 across paths; PU→ATT β=0.208; PEOU→ATT β=0.228

finding.finding_summary: The paper emphasizes engagement, learner-interface interactivity, and attitude formation as key outcomes of using GenAI in K-12 AI education. Students rated the course and GenAI-supported learning positively, and the model showed that perceived usefulness and ease of use significantly predicted attitudes toward the AI course (PU→ATT β=0.208; PEOU→ATT β=0.228) in the valid sample of n=197.
finding.measure: Attitudes toward AI course learning; perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use as proximal engagement-related outcomes
